slides.title: Employee General Safety Training Overview
slides.description:
Hazard Communication Standard (Employee Right-to-Know)

The purpose of the OSHA’s Hazard Communication Standard (HCS) (also called the employee right-to-know) is to provide employees with information pertaining to potential exposures to the dangers of hazardous materials in the workplace.

slides.title: Safety Philosophy
slides.description:
All injuries can be prevented or greatly reduced, all employees including managers and owners are responsible for preventing occupational injuries and illnesses.

Every effort must be made to safeguard all operating conditions that may potentially injure technicians, mechanics and other shop personnel (as well as customers and visitors) or damage property and equipment.

Learning to work and behave safely is an on-going and important part of your shop’s operation.

Working safely is the only right way of operating a shop. In the long run, it is also more cost-effective.

Accidents are caused by unsafe conditions and/or unsafe behaviors.

slides.title: Types of Unsafe Conditions and Behavior in the Shop
slides.description:
Improper rails and machine guarding

Improper lighting and ventilation

Hazardous protective equipment or apparel

Defective tools, machines, and working surfaces

Failure to used proper PPE (Personal Protective Equipment)

Unsafe positions and postures including loading, carrying and lifting

Using unsafe equipment, using equipment unsafely and making safety devices inoperative.

Moving dangerous equipment without proper training/help

Operating equipment without authority and or operating at unsafe speeds

Failure to secure objects, use lockout procedures and warn others or give proper signals Distractions and or Horseplay

slides.title: Basic Shop Safety Rules
slides.description:
Keep your work area clean

Neatly arrange equipment and material. Do not allow parts, metal, wires, scrapes or small material to accumulate on the shop floor or in your work areas. Place drink cups, cans, bottles, paper, lunch scraps, etc. in the proper containers.

Report every injury to your supervisor, no matter how slight or insignificant the injury may seem.

Request assistance from your supervisor if you are insure about the safe operation or process of the job.

Report un-safe conditions to your supervisor immediately. Rely on your judgment and knowledge of safety to guide you.

Horseplay is forbidden do not interfere with co-workers when they are performing their job, no running except in emergencies.

Be certain all safety guards are in place before operating any machine or equipment.

Check for the safety and clearance of all personnel before energizing or operating any machine hoist or other equipment.

slides.title: Basic Shop Safety Rules
slides.description:
All equipment must be locked out prior to any repairs or maintenance. Lock Outs my only be removed by authorized personnel/management.

Never work on an electrical system under unsafe conditions. Pull the switch controlling the machine insuring it’s turned off. Allow equipment to come to full stop and then lock and tag it. Push start button insuring the machine is definitely off.

Never tie down, block out or otherwise make inoperative any type of safety device, attachment, method or guard.

Observe all caution and danger signs

Never oil, remove guards or attempt to repair machinery while it is in motion. Do not climb on machinery while oiling or greasing.

Do not use electrical equipment while standing in damp or wet surfaced or when your hands are wet.

Only electricians or authorized personnel are permitted to perform electrical work.

PPE required in each shop must be worn as specified. Safety-toe shoes, bump hats, safety glasses with sideshields, goggles, faceshields, respirators and other forms of protective equipment or clothing are for employee protection.

Gloves should not be worn when operating drills, lathes or other types of machinery that contain rotating spindles or cutting tools.

slides.title: Basic Shop Safety Rules
slides.description:
Wear clothes that are suitable for work

Working without shirts is not permitted. Long-sleeve shirts must be worn when burning, welding, grinding or performing other types of work where sparks or hot metal are present, acids or similar substances.

Neckties, rings, watches and loose or ragged clothing create hazards. Do not wear.

Lift objects with your legs not your backs. Keep backs straight.

Observe “No Smoking Areas” Never smoke near the following: compressed gas cylinders (oxygen-gas). Paint operation, flammable storage rooms, near gasoline or fuel stations etc.

Wipe up immediately any oil spills, grease, paint or any other slippery substance to prevent a fall.

Approved safety cans must be used for flammable liquids such as gasoline, solvents and thinners.

Know where your fire extinguishers are located. In case of a fire first pull the fire alarm.

Never use an air hose for cleaning yourself off. Approved safety guns must not exceed 30 (psi)

Never stack material or product so that obstructs safety equipment, aisles, ladders, steps, electrical boxes, etc.

Stay clear of objects being moved or handled by any type of conveyance when storing material.

questions.question: All injuries can be prevented or greatly reduced, and all employees (including managers and owners) are responsible for preventing occupational injuries and illnesses.
Which statement best matches the training’s safety philosophy?

answers.a: Safety is optional if you are experienced
answers.b: Working safely is the only right way to operate a shop and is more cost-effective long term
answers.c: Accidents are unavoidable in shop work
answers.d: Only supervisors are responsible for safety

questions.question: Which is an example of an unsafe condition or behavior in the shop?
Horseplay is forbidden, and you should not interfere with co-workers while they are working.
What must be done before any repairs or maintenance on equipment?

answers.a: Oil the machine while it is running
answers.b: Lock out the equipment; lockouts removed only by authorized personnel/management
answers.c: Test-run the machine at a low speed
answers.d: Remove safety guards for easier access

questions.question: Only electricians or authorized personnel are permitted to perform electrical work.
Which clothing or accessory creates a hazard and should not be worn in the shop?

answers.c: Neckties, rings, watches, or loose/ragged clothing

questions.question: What is the safest way to lift heavy objects?

answers.a: Bend at the waist and lift with your back
answers.b: Lift with your legs and keep your back straight
answers.c: Twist while lifting to reposition quickly
